extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of poetry, literary criticism, and philosophy of mind; writers interested in imagination, memory, and literary authenticity
extracted.subtask_description: The excerpt discusses the cognitive and moral conditions that underlie imagination, memory, and genuine literary expression, offering prescriptive remarks useful to poets and creative writers about how to cultivate and evaluate imagination, memory, and authenticity in literary work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination (poetry) — superior degree plus voluntary control
rubrics_metrics.description: The IMAGINATION is an intermediate faculty that is at once both active and passive. In common language, and especially on the subject of poetry, the name is appropriated to a superior degree of the faculty, joined to a superior voluntary control over it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For poetic production, imagination is not merely associative happenstance but requires cultivated, voluntary control: the poet should develop the capacity to direct and intensify the imagination deliberately (i.e., deliberate attention and control over associative processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Will/Attention to intensify vividness
rubrics_metrics.description: The will itself by confining and intensifying the attention may arbitrarily give vividness or distinctness to any object whatsoever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises active mental discipline: a writer can make particular images or ideas more vivid through focused attention. This is a practical technique for crafting memorable imagery and for recalling material while composing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of likeness and contrast for associative recall
rubrics_metrics.description: An idea may be recalled either by contemporaneity (co-presence) or by the joint operation of likeness and contrast — e.g., seeing a mackerel may make one think of gooseberries (by association), then goose, then swan by likeness and contrast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing associative sequences, employ both similarity and contrast to move the reader’s mind between images and ideas plausibly; this models natural associative thought and can produce surprising but coherent poetic transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneity/continuity as condition of association
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporaneity (co-presence in time) is the common condition of all the laws of association; nothing that forms parts of a total impression can be associated unless co-present in some sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In composition and memory techniques, ensure elements you wish to link are presented with sufficient temporal or contextual co-presence so that readers (or your own memory) will form the intended associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts of Memory — sound logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound logic is listed among 'the best, the only Arts of Memory.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate logical organization and clarity of thought as foundational to reliable recall and to constructing persuasive, memorable literary argument or narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts of Memory — philosophical knowledge of facts under cause and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophical knowledge of facts under the relation of cause and effect is an essential art of memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding causal relations between facts strengthens one’s capacity to remember and to assemble coherent narrative or argument; knowledge organized by causality is more retrievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts of Memory — cheerful and communicative temper
rubrics_metrics.description: A cheerful and communicative temper disposing us to notice similarities and contrasts is among the best Arts of Memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An open, sociable disposition promotes noticing connections between things — a useful habit for generating associations, metaphors, and analogies in creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts of Memory — quiet conscience and freedom from anxieties
rubrics_metrics.description: A quiet conscience and a condition free from anxieties are necessary Arts of Memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional tranquility aids recollection and imaginative work; personal or moral unease can impede the mind’s associative and recollective functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arts of Memory — sound health and healthy digestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound health, and above all (as far as relates to passive remembrance) a healthy digestion, are the best, the only Arts of Memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical well-being (including digestion) is explicitly recommended as necessary for reliable memory and creative functioning—practical reminder that bodily state affects literary productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject artificial mnemonic schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain recent schemes promising an artificial memory are useless, if not absurd; they can only produce confusion and debasement of the fancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-reliance on contrived mnemonic tricks that replace genuine associative and imaginative habits; prefer cultivation of natural mental faculties and healthy conditions over mechanical shortcuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of latent sensory relics and textual echoes for verisimilitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Relics of sensation may exist for an indefinite time in a latent state, and passages read or heard long before can reappear in feverish states as exact impressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting dreams, hallucinations, or recollections, grounding them in plausible prior sensory/textual impressions (echoes of reading, spoken texts) increases credibility; textual echoes can explain uncanny accuracy of remembered material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity through immediate echo of feeling over polished orthography
rubrics_metrics.description: The unlearned, in simplicity of soul, made their words immediate echoes of their feelings; by contrast the literati could write orthographically and make smooth periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuing immediacy of feeling and directness of expression can produce more authentic and inspired writing than excessive polish alone; cultivated smoothness should not suppress the immediacy of genuine emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware literary 'tacit compact' that limits free thought
rubrics_metrics.description: There appears to have existed a tacit compact among the learned not to pass beyond a certain limit in speculative science; free thought was constrained and those who overstepped were persecuted or avoided the appearance of doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should recognize institutional and social limits on acceptable speculation; genuine originality may require modesty or discretion in presentation, and awareness that transgressive thought may attract censure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility about method — do not mistake conditions for causes
rubrics_metrics.description: The common sophism is mistaking the conditions of a thing for its causes and essence; the process by which we arrive at the knowledge of a faculty is not the faculty itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In creative theory and craft, distinguish between the external conditions that facilitate artistic activity (health, memory aids) and the essence of the creative faculty; avoid conflating a technique with the underlying power it supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral improvement often precedes intellectual improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Such men need discipline, not argument; they must be made better men before they can become wiser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author suggests moral cultivation and character formation are prerequisites for genuine intellectual and artistic advancement—ethical self-discipline may be part of becoming a better writer.
